newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WORLD SERIES CHAMPION BRAVES CLINCH NL EAST PENNANT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WORLD SERIES CHAMPION BRAVES CLINCH NL EAST PENNANT.

text.p: Top Cy Young Award candidate John Smoltz led the way as the defending World Series champion Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East title with an 8-2 victory over the Montreal Expos on Sunday.

Smoltz, baseball's best pitcher in 1996, improved to 23-8, allowing two runs and four hits over eight innings with 10 strikeouts. He assured himself of his 23rd victory with his bat, belting a three-run homer off Jeff Fassero (15-10) in the sixth inning.
The win marks the fifth straight division title for the Braves, who are favoured to return to the World Series.

"I just feel like this has been a year that I have been blessed with in many ways," said Smoltz, who ran his league-leading strikeout total to 272, breaking the club record set by Phil Niekro in 1977.
"It's just been an amazing year for me personally. I'll never forget this home run," Smoltz said.
After a slide that saw them lose 11 of 13 games, the Braves have turned things around, winning seven of eight.
In San Diego, Steve Finley hit a two-run homer to lift the Padres to a crucial 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
San Diego earned a split of the key four-game series to pull back to within a half game of first-place Los Angeles in the West Division title race.
The Padres scored all of their runs in the fifth against Hideo Nomo (16-11), who was coming off a no-hitter.
Rickey Henderson and Tony Gwynn hit back-to-back doubles to tie the game at 1-1 tie before Finley hit his 28th homer.
Andy Ashby (9-5) gave up one run and seven hits in five innings for the victory.
In Cincinnati, the Reds swept a double header from St Louis, preventing the Cardinals from capturing the Central Division title.
Bret Boone triggered a four-run seventh with a two-run triple and five relievers combined to pitch five scoreless innings as the Reds rallied for a 6-3 win in the opener.
The Cardinals carried a 3-2 lead into the bottom of the seventh, but the Reds scored four runs with two outs against T.J. Mathews (2-6). Jeff Shaw (8-5) pitched two scoreless innings for the victory.
In the second game, John Smiley fired a one-hitter, facing one batter over the minimum, and added a two-run single to cap a five-run first inning as the Reds blanked the Cardinals 6-0.
Smiley (13-14) retired the first nine batters before Royce Clayton led off the fourth with a single. Smiley then set down the next 18 batters in a row.
The Cardinals' magic number dropped to two, however, when second-place Houston lost again.
At Florida, Rick Helling took a no-hitter into the seventh inning and Andre Dawson belted a pinch-hit three-run homer to lead the Marlins to a 6-0 blanking of the reeling Astros.
Helling (2-1) did not allow a hit until Craig Biggio led off the seventh with a line single to centre. It was the only hit he surrendered in eight innings.
The Marlins gave Helling all the support he needed with three runs in the first against Darryl Kile (12-10) as Houston lost its eighth in a row and 12th straight on the road.
In Pittsburgh, Jay Bell continued his torrid hitting with a homer and four RBI to lead the Pirates to a major-league best 11th straight win, an 11-3 drubbing of the Chicago Cubs.
The Pirates, in last place in the Central Division, have been on a tear since manager Jim Leyland announced his intentions not to return next season.
The Pirates scored five times in the top of the first and never looked back. Bell extended his hitting streak to 14 games and homered for the third game in a row.
Francisco Cordova (4-7) gave up three runs and five hits in five innings to get the win.

In San Francisco, Glenallen Hill hit a three-run homer in the first inning and drove in four runs and Steve Soderstrom pitched seven strong innings as the Giants completed a four-game sweep of the Colorado Rockies with a 7-3 victory.
The Rockies scored three runs in the top of the first, but the Giants answered with four in their half of the inning against David Nied (0-1), capped by Hill's 18th home run.
Hill's sacrifice fly in the fourth extended San Francisco's lead to 6-3.
Soderstrom (1-0), making his second major-league start, allowed three runs and six hits.
In Philadelphia, Gregg Jefferies blooped a double down the left-field line in the bottom of the ninth to score Desi Relaford with the winning run as the Phillies edged the New York Mets 4-3.
Rookie Derek Wallace (2-2) gave up the winning hit to suffer the loss. Rickey Bottalico (4-5) worked a scoreless ninth for the victory.
New York's Lance Johnson went 1-for-5 for his major-league leading 219th hit of the season. It is the most hits in a season since Pete Rose had 230 in 1973.
